title: RTEC sexual-harassment reporting, complaint form and investigation authority map

rules: Sexual harassment is unacceptable and harassing conduct is subject to discipline.
The handbook describes both quid-pro-quo-type conduct and hostile/intimidating/offensive-environment conduct.
An employee experiencing sexual harassment is encouraged to report/discuss it with a supervisor, Human Resource Manager, or Executive Director.

fields: dates and nature of alleged conduct
investigation_statement: The form states that investigation requires interviewing the complainant, alleged harasser(s), and witnesses with knowledge of allegations or defenses.
The form states that persons involved will be told the investigation is confidential and that unauthorized disclosure could lead to discipline up to discharge.

historical_aap_context: The 2015-2018 AAP says employees experiencing sexual harassment are encouraged to discuss the situation with their supervisor, EEO Manager, Human Resource Manager or Executive Director.
The historical AAP states that a Sexual Harassment Complaint Form is available from the EEO Manager.
The AAP prohibits threats, intimidation and retaliation against a person for reporting sexual harassment or helping another person bring a complaint.
current_process_model: Receive a report through any current handbook-authorized reporting channel.

Move case-specific allegations, identities, evidence, medical expense information and interview notes into restricted case storage immediately; do not place those facts in generalized GitHub knowledge.
Confirm the person responsible for investigating under current RTEC authority and identify any conflicts of interest before assignment.
Preserve relevant documents/evidence and identify the complainant, accused person(s), witnesses and relevant time period.
Conduct fact-finding interviews and document allegations, responses and supporting evidence.
Determine findings and necessary corrective/disciplinary action through the current authorized decision path.
Communicate the result/next-step information appropriate under current RTEC policy and retain the restricted case record.
Apply the current anti-retaliation requirement throughout and after the investigation.
authority_conflicts_and_gaps: The current 2025 handbook provides reporting routes but does not, in the ingested text, expressly adopt the 2017 complaint form or its detailed investigation language.
The 2017 form must therefore remain a historical template until a newer/current form or explicit adoption is found.
Historical AAP references to named EEO managers are superseded by later officer/role assignments and must not control current routing.
A current RTEC-specific investigation SOP, decision authority, target timelines, appeal/review process and retention schedule have not yet been established from the ingested current sources.
privacy_controls: Harassment complaints are restricted employee-relations case records.
Do not persist complainant, accused, witness, medical, evidence or outcome details in generalized process knowledge.
Generalized records may store blank form structure, workflow, policy authority, non-identifying aggregate statistics and provenance.
automation_candidates: Restricted harassment/employee-relations case intake with role-based access.
Evidence/interview checklist and anti-retaliation follow-up reminders.
Current-form version control so historical complaint forms cannot be accidentally reused as current.
Aggregate case metrics that exclude identities and allegations.
